sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Where the place data comes from
sections.what: Brings in the career entries so that each role's project locations can be looked up. The file header explains the rule: cities mark where a role was based, and countries and regions mark where the work was.
sections.why: Likely reason: the project locations already live in the career data, so this file reads them there rather than repeating them.
sections.watch_out: This file loads the career data when it starts, so a mistake in battles.ts also breaks this file.

sections.name: Place
sections.title: Shape of a map location
sections.what: Describes one place as a display label plus a latitude and longitude, which give the position of its marker on the globe.
sections.why: Likely reason: each globe marker needs a name and a position, so both are kept together.
sections.watch_out: Coordinates are typed by hand and never checked, so a swapped or mistyped number puts the marker in the wrong place.

sections.name: places
sections.title: Named locations for globe markers
sections.what: Lists the cities, countries and regions the globes can show, each with a name and a position. Country and region markers sit on a rough centre rather than an office.
sections.why: Likely reason: one shared list lets several career entries use the same location key.
sections.watch_out: A key used in the career data but missing here is quietly dropped from the globe rather than reported as an error.

sections.name: roleBase
sections.title: Home base for each career entry
sections.what: Records the city where each career entry was based, for example Gurugram for the Bain role. It also builds, from the career data, one list of places for each key project of each entry.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code for keeping home base here, although the career data also has a location field.
sections.watch_out: The home base is typed here separately from the location field in the career data, so the two can disagree without any error.

sections.name: rolePlaces
sections.title: Places to show for one role
sections.what: Returns the distinct places a career entry touched, with its home base first, as a list ready to draw on the globe. Places that cannot be found in the places list are removed.
sections.why: Likely reason: the globe needs one clean list per role, with no duplicates and no missing entries.
sections.watch_out: If a role has no home base entry, its base is silently skipped and only its project places appear.

summary: Holds the map locations for the globes and works out which places each career entry touched.
purpose: Feeds the globe markers with names and positions for each role.
why: The file's header says cities are where a role was based, and countries and regions are where the client work was.
how: First, the career data is loaded. Then places are defined with a name and a position. Each role's home base is recorded. Place lists are built from the project locations in the career data. Finally, a function returns a clean list of places for a role.
inputs: The career data in battles.ts for project locations, and the hand-typed home base list.
outputs: The places lookup, the home base list, the per-role project place lists, and the function that returns a role's places for the globe.
risks: Latitude and longitude are typed by hand and not checked, so a swapped pair puts a marker in the wrong place. Unknown place keys are dropped silently. The home base list can disagree with the location field in the career data.
debug: If a marker is missing, check that the location key in the career data exists in the places list. If a role has no home marker, check that it appears in the home base list. If a marker is in the wrong spot, check the order of latitude and longitude.
